page: Microsoft Azure D2pds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the ARM64 processor architecture and managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The server does not include GPU acceleration hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Storage configuration includes 118 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, providing low-latency ephemeral disk space directly connected to the host. The instance is also capable of attaching Azure Premium Storage volumes for external persistent workloads requiring reliable block storage.

The use of ARM64 cores provides energy-efficient compute capacity for multi-threaded services. Qualitative cost efficiency is realized through the density of the 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio paired with fast local scratch storage. However, applications requiring x86-specific instruction sets cannot run without recompilation or emulation.

Microsoft Azure D2pds_v7 is suited for balanced general-purpose workloads, including containerized microservices, light web applications, software build nodes, and small caching databases that benefit from high-speed local NVMe storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D2pds_v7 is an ARM64-based general-purpose virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The integrated NVMe drive supplies high-throughput, low-latency ephemeral storage for temporary application data and caching. Microsoft Azure D2pds_v7 is engineered for general-purpose workloads, including small databases, web application backends, lightweight caching layers, and continuous integration pipelines.
